identity.title: A Kinematical Detection of Two Embedded Jupiter-mass Planets in HD 163296

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using archival ALMA observations of HD 163296, we demonstrate a new technique to measure the rotation curves of CO isotopologue emission to sub-percent precision relative to the Keplerian rotation.

question.value: Can precise rotation curves of CO isotopologue emission reveal pressure-gradient perturbations from embedded planets in the HD 163296 disk?

evidence.quote: In this Letter we present a new method to precisely measure $v_{\rm rot}$ which is used to make the first kinematical detection of embedded planets in the disk of HD 163296

analysis_steps.goal: Derive rotation velocity profile by stacking deprojected spectra

method.value: Annuli ~2 pixels wide (~9 au); shift spectra by v_rot cos(theta), stack; the correct v_rot minimizes stacked line width

evidence.quote: We assert that the correct $v_{\rm rot}$ is the value which minimizes this width.

evidence.quote: For a SNR of $\gtrsim 10$, as with the observations, we could recover $v_{\rm rot}$ accurately to a precision of $2~{\rm m\,s^{-1}}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Run hydrodynamic simulations and synthetic C18O observations

findings_qualitative.value: Rotation curves show deviations centred on continuum gaps, consistent with pressure-gradient perturbations; density changes dominate over temperature or height

evidence.quote: the dominant source of the perturbation is changes in the density profile, consistent with the previously proposed embedded planet scenario

claims.hypothesis: Embedded planets cause detectable velocity deviations in the gas rotation
claims.experiment: Measured C18O rotation curve and compared with 2D hydro+LIME models
claims.result: 1 MJup at 100 au and 1.3 MJup at 165 au match observed delta v_rot
claims.finding: Kinematical detection of two Jupiter-mass planets

evidence.quote: Comparisons with hydrodynamic models found excellent agreement with a $1~M_{\rm Jup}$ planet at 100 au and a $1.3~M_{\rm Jup}$ at 165 au

claims.hypothesis: The inner perturbation is explained by a single planet
claims.finding: Inner feature unresolved; alternatives such as pressure confinement possible

evidence.quote: were unable to find a convincing fit to the feature at $< 70$ au

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Vertical shear instability, ambipolar diffusion and magnetic reconnection rejected or unsupported for outer gaps

evidence.quote: For the outer two perturbations, only the embedded planet scenario is able to succinctly account for all the observations.

limitations_admitted.value: No gap cooling included, so planet masses are upper limits; planet not directly detected

evidence.quote: our planet masses should be seen as an upper limit
without the detection of a point source, we cannot unambiguously dismiss scenarios without a planet
